articles.title: Ben Shelton dethrones Carlos Alcaraz in five-set thriller after latest US Open finish
articles.summary: Winner claims 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (7) victory. Epic quarter-final ends after 3.30am in New York. As the official 10th day of play in New York moved deeper into the remote hours of the new morning, every passing game imbued Carlos Alcaraz with greater despair.
body: Instead, the contest would develop into one of the most remarkable matches of the year as Alcaraz dragged himself into a fifth set and came so close to orchestrating another seemingly impossible comeback. This time, he was denied by a brave, defiant Shelton, who refused to be shaken by the status of his rival or the prospect of securing the greatest win of career after four hours and 29 minutes on court. At 3.33am, the sun not long from rising over Flushing Meadows yet a half-full Arthur Ashe Stadium still hollering until the end, Shelton closed out with a 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (7) win over Alcaraz to reach the semi-finals of the US Open.

Two days after dominating Tommy Paul, another American, this match was a far more faithful reflection of how challenging it is for Alcaraz to play under such high pressure and intensity with so few matches under his belt. Shelton managed the moment and occasion spectacularly remaining consistent across five sets and soaking up so much pressure in the fifth set. Most importantly, he held his nerve until the end.

articles.title: Dani Olmo: ‘Winning the World Cup changes you, it changes your life’
articles.summary: One of Barcelona’s eight World Cup winners reflects on how Spain’s triumph is inspiring them in the Champions League. Dani Olmo nods towards his right arm. “Look: goosebumps,” he says.
body: But then Olmo knew, felt it: Spain were world champions. It was 19 July in New Jersey and it was real: Spain had beaten Argentina and nothing would be the same again.

So now it’s time to, well, to get back to work, another generation to emulate. Twenty-three days after victory in the US, Olmo was back where he sits now, another session complete, another European season about to start. His club coach was waiting.
What did Hansi Flick say? “‘You’re a champion of the world, Dani.’” “‘I know, mister.’” Olmo laughs at what came next. “And now [we have to do it] with Barcelona,” he says.

Eight of Spain’s 26-man squad were Barcelona players and although Maria’s son Ferran has departed for Paris Saint German, Rodri has joined from Manchester City. What they have done with their country can infuse club success, Olmo believes, just as what they do with their club infused success with the country. Winning the World Cup changes your life; it can also reinforce an idea, and while Olmo analyses the differences between Spain and Barcelona, Flick and Luis de la Fuente, this is the triumph of an idea, continuity and commitment.

articles.title: Shelton beats Alcaraz in latest-ever US Open finish to reach semis
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence is over after a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton that ends at 03:34 local time in New York.
body: Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence came to an end in a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton that ended at 03:34 local time - the latest finish in the tournament's history.
A large crowd remained captivated deep into the night as a modern classic unfolded over an unpredictable four hours and 28 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium.
The match did not begin until about 11pm in New York, after the start of the night session was delayed by Tuesday's earlier matches.

At its conclusion, eighth seed Shelton basked in a standing ovation from a delirious audience after completing a 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) victory that will live long in the memory of all those still present.

articles.title: Football’s most damaging red cards: a brief history of collapses and turnarounds | The Knowledge
articles.summary: Plus: clubs with multiple £100m players on their books and more trophy-laden footballers. Mail us with your all of your questions and answers. “The Saturday before last, Clyde were winning 3-0 at The Spartans after an hour when Logan Dunachie was sent off.
body: At Knowledge Towers, we usually receive questions about the greatest comebacks with 10 men. We covered that in 2021, so it’s a nice change to look at teams who went to seed after having a player sent off.

Before we get to the meat of the question, a quick detour to cover some teams who were already losing and then fell apart completely after losing a player. There are examples dotted throughout the Premier League era. At the Etihad in 2017-18, Liverpool were a goal down to Manchester City when Sadio Mané was sent off in the 37th minute for a high challenge on Ederson. They lost 5-0.

Two seasons later, Southampton were 1-0 down at home to Leicester when Ryan Bertrand was sent off in the 12th minute. They were eventually humiliated 9-0. VVV-Venlo went one worse against Ajax the following season. They were 4-0 down at home when Christian Kum was sent off in the 52nd minute. By the hour mark it was 8-0; Ajax eventually won 13-0.

articles.title: More than a game: NFL hopes Melbourne visit will advance case for Olympic flag football
articles.summary: NFL executives use this week to push for inclusion at Brisbane 2032. Possibility a key reason Melbourne secured Rams v 49ers match. The NFL’s regular season debut in Australia will deliver a significant commercial return for the league and its clubs, but the league’s takeover of Melbourne this week…
body: The scheduling of Friday’s match at the MCG is also designed to help secure a place for flag football – a non-contact version of American football – at the Brisbane Olympics.

The IOC is finalising the core disciplines for the 2032 Games this year, before local organisers can propose additional sports. The process is expected to be completed before the end of the year or early 2027.
Flag football will make its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles and NFL executives have used this week’s visit to advance the case for the sport’s inclusion at Brisbane.

“Flag football is a huge part of our effort,” NFL’s executive vice president for international events, Peter O’Reilly, told the SportNXT conference on Tuesday. “[It’s] one of the fastest-growing sports in the world, [we’re] excited for it to be on the sport program for LA 28 [and] very hopeful it’s on for Brisbane 32.”

articles.title: England to extend head coach Borthwick's contract
articles.summary: England head coach Steve Borthwick will have his contract extended past the 2028 Six Nations in a bid to avoid uncertainty over his future before and during next year's Rugby World Cup.
body: As it did with Red Roses boss John Mitchell before the 2025 World Cup, the Rugby Football Union has moved to ensure Borthwick and his staff have some clarity over their positions going into the global showpiece.
According to RFU performance director Conor O'Shea, extending Borthwick's deal into the middle of 2028 will allow time to decide who leads the team in the longer-term.
"You don't want them looking for a job going into [a World Cup]," O'Shea explained.
"Everyone knows it will be judged on the World Cup, but you can't have a group of coaches going in with that uncertainty, especially when you look at the timing.

articles.title: See the uniforms Rutgers football will wear to honor lives lost on 9/11
articles.summary: PISCATAWAY – Greg Schiano was in his first year as Rutgers football’s head coach when the tragic events of Sept. 11, 2001 occurred. “This is very real to us,” Schiano said Tuesday at his news conference to preview his team’s next game against Boston College.
body: It’s for that reason that anytime Schiano’s team has a chance to play on Sept. 11 and honor the lives would were lost, it’s significant.

The Scarlet Knights will play the Eagles at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts in the Red Bandanna Game, which honors Boston College alumnus Welles Crowther, who died while saving 12 people in the South Tower of the World Trade Center.

“Welles Crowther is one of the many heroes that stood up on 9/11,” Schiano said. “The stories are legendary of him carrying people out of the building. People owe their lives to him. There’s a lot of those people.”
Rutgers during the game will wear special uniforms that honor the tragic events of 9/11 and the 37 alumni who lost their lives on that day.

articles.title: England to make major change to kit after striking sponsorship deal with Lloyds Bank
articles.summary: The back of England rugby ’s shirts will carry a sponsor’s name for the first time after Lloyds Bank struck a lucrative new partnership with the Rugby Football Union (RFU).
body: The multi-million pound per year deal will see the bank’s famous black horse logo and name emblazoned above the player names on the kits of England’s men and women, beginning with the Red Roses’ clash with Australia in Manchester this weekend.
The agreement will see Lloyds becomes one of the RFU’s leading partners, with significant investment expected into the community game, and is another significant boost to the union’s finances.
O2 have been England’s front-of-shirt sponsor for 30 years, while Allianz took the naming rights to Twickenham in 2024 in a 10-year sponsorship deal.

“This is a truly significant partnership for the RFU and marks an important moment for rugby in England. Lloyds is one of the country’s most recognised and proudly British brands, and their commitment extends far beyond visibility on the England shirt,” RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney said.

articles.title: Shelton beats Alcaraz at 3.33am in New York epic
articles.summary: Ben Shelton clinched the biggest win of his career as he defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set epic stretching deep into the New York night to reach the semi-finals of the US Open.
body: The American prevailed 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-1 1-6 7-6 (10-7) over four hours and 28 minutes to reward a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd gripped until 3.33am in what was the latest-ever finish to a US Open match.
It marked Shelton's first career win over a top-three player, against which he had been 0-17 coming into the match.
Shelton will now play Frances Tiafoe in the final four after his fellow countryman's thrilling five-set victory over Alex Michelsen earlier in the evening.

"For me it's always about the people in the crowd, whether it's my coaches, team or friends and family, or the city of New York that showed up tonight until 3am with the USA chants, that's what kept me going and what got me this win," Shelton said on-court.

articles.title: F1's toughest street track ever? Why new Madring could cause Spanish GP chaos
articles.summary: Formula 1 has a brand-new track to look forward to this weekend and the expectation is there will be carnage and the drivers will be seriously tested at the Madring.
body: The Spanish Grand Prix has moved from its traditional circuit in Barcelona to a high-speed street track in Madrid and has been described as "Jeddah on steroids" by Formula 3 drivers who tested there last month - the Jeddah track itself is one of the most challenging circuits in F1.
So why is the Madring so difficult and how will it impact the racing we see this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1?
There are 22 official corners on the 3.365-mile Madring circuit, although unusually the track layout has Turns 5A and 20A - so maybe there are 24.
Whatever the number, after the start/finish straight the driver will almost always be turning the steering wheel at some point as there are few straights.

articles.title: From honeymoon vision to the Super Bowl - can Seahawks win it all again?
articles.summary: Honeymoons are for newlyweds celebrating true love and for future NFL head coaches plotting Super Bowl glory. At least in the case of Mike Macdonald, who has now turned to the Chicago Bulls as his recipe reference for a repeat.
body: Mystic Macdonald went viral earlier this year when the Seattle Seahawks released footage of his first-ever team meeting upon being appointed in 2024. Within it, he had strayed from his script to forecast a place at the NFC Championship Game and an 'inevitable' feel to a 'won't die, won't quit' machine.
"It probably came to me about 30 minutes before the meeting," Macdonald tells Sky Sports of his viral speech.
Between some fine fortune-telling and a relentless winning formula, that vision became a reality 21 months later as Seattle beat the Los Angeles Rams to reach Super Bowl LX.

It would eventually culminate in Macdonald's skyward gaze towards the cloud of confetti and fireworks honouring his Seahawks as NFL champions following their victory over the New England Patriots at Levi's Stadium in February.
